chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Rifa'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), so I said, 'I buy a slave girl, and she stays with me for months and does not menstruate, and that is not due to old age. So I show her to the women, and they say, 'She is not pregnant.' So, is it permissible for me to have intercourse with her in her private part?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Menstruation can be withheld by the wind without pregnancy. So there is no problem if you touch her in the private part.' I said, 'But if she is pregnant, what is for me from her, if I intend?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is besides the private part.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a man to have sexual intercourse with a female slave who has not menstruated?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) addresses the specific legal nuance of *tamkin* (availability) for a female slave (*umm walad* or *jariya*) who has not yet menstruated. He clarifies that amenorrhea can be caused by factors other than pregnancy, such as wind, thereby permitting the owner to engage in vaginal intercourse; however, if she is indeed pregnant, his right is restricted to the vagina, excluding other forms of intimacy or full marital rights.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Rifa’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘I bought a slave girl, so she remained with me for the month and did not menstruate, and that was not due to old age. So I showed her to the women, and they said, ‘She is not with a pregnancy’. So, is it for me that I sleep in her private part?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wind could have withheld the menstruation from without a pregnancy. So there is no problem if you were to touch her in the private part’. I said, ‘Supposing she was pregnant, so what would be for me from her, if I intend?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever is besides the private part’.
